name: Cen
world_status: accessible description is silent on stress

earlier_scan.source_named: Glottolog lists only Gerhardt 2011 subclassification comment; no grammar, phonology or sketch named

sources.citation: OLAC: 'OLAC resources in and about the Cen language' (language-archives.org/language/cen, Internet Archive copy 2023-07-14).
sources.note: Catalogue only: lists nothing but the Glottolog 4.7 and Ethnologue entries for [cen]; no descriptions, texts or lexica.

sources.citation: Blench, Roger M. & Bitrus Bulus Kaze. 2019. Izere Dictionary composite 2019 (rogerblench.info, Izeric/Language/Izere Dictionary composite).
sources.note: Updated version of the Izere dictionary whose introduction covers Izeric dialects incl. Cen; could add prosodic remarks beyond the 2006 intro (which has tone only). Closest-relative evidence, not Cen itself.

sources.citation: Wikipedia, 'Izere language' (Cen language redirects here), accessed 2026-09-17.
sources.note: Phonology section is for Izere (from Blench & Kaze): three tone levels plus two rare contour tones; nothing on stress; nothing Cen-specific beyond Berom-derived prefixes/consonant alternation.

sources.citation: Blench, Roger M. 2009. The Cen language of Central Nigeria and its affinities. Draft circulated for comment (printout July 10, 2009). Cambridge: Kay Williamson Educational Foundation. 12 pp.
sources.note: Nothing. Sec. 3 'Phonology' (pp. 2-3), explicitly 'based on rapid observations.. tentative', contains only 3.1 Vowels (seven-vowel chart) and 3.2 Consonants (chart); no section or sentence on tone, stress or accent. The English-Cen/Cen-English wordlist (pp. 4-11) is tone-marked with acute/grave/macron/circumflex/caron diacritics, implying a lexical-tone analysis, but no prose statement is given.

sources.citation: ISO 639-3 Registration Authority. 2007. Change Request 2006-083 (create [cen] Cen) and accompanying Request for New Language Code Element 'cen'. SIL International.
sources.note: Nothing; sociolinguistic/identification data only (2000 speakers, ~5 villages around Duruk Kamang SE of Jos; closest language Izere; source = Blench survey e-mail 2003). Section 5c 'published sources' left blank, i.e. no grammar or dictionary known to the requesters.

sources.citation: Blench, Roger M. & Bitrus Bulus Kaze. 2006. A dictionary of the Izere language of Fobur: Introduction. Cambridge, unpublished ms., 20 pp.
sources.note: Describes Ibor (Fobur) Izere, the closest relative, not Cen. Sec. 3.1 treats Cen (Aficen, Foron area) as a Southern Izeric variety. Sec. 4.1 (p. 9-10): 'Izere has 29 consonant phonemes, 7 vowel phonemes and 3 level tones'.. 'There are five tones in Izere, three level and two contour tones (LM & HL).. Izere can be regarded as having an underlying three-height system.' No mention of stress or accent anywhere.

sources.citation: Blench, Roger M. n.d. The strange case of Ganang. 1 p. note, rogerblench.info (Izeric/Dialects).
sources.note: Nothing; sociolinguistic note on Ganang only, Cen not discussed.

sources.citation: Cen Literacy Committee / Andy Kellogg (SIL Nigeria), c. 2009-: Cen (Icen) orthography statement, alphabet/reading-and-writing materials or phonology sketch produced at the Jos workshops mentioned in Blench 2009 (unpublished; existence not verified).
sources.tag: likely states stress; not yet obtained
sources.note: Blench 2009 reports an active Cen literacy committee working with SIL's Andy Kellogg; any orthography statement would normally include a tone/stress section and would be the first prosodic statement for Cen.
